title: Jimmy Blanton, Oscar Pettiford and the bass becoming a solo instrument
summary: Bass had been a section instrument.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

As far as solo bass, I guess the
guy that really turned it all around was Jimmy Blanton.

That's another guy that just
suddenly appeared.

I remember him in Kansas City. Jimmy
Blanton, and there was -- I'm trying to think of this bass
player, well, outside of Oscar Pettiford in Minneapolis. He
was another one.

Yeah. Didn't one of his brothers
play with Earl's band? Trumpet playing brother?

I don't know. Maybe in later years,
but not while I was with the band.

Yeah, Oscar and -- I guess Blanton
was first, and then Oscar.

Yeah. And then there was another
bass player up in Minneapolis played the same kind of bass.
Adolphus, I can't think of his full name.
late thirties, you know, the bass had always been just a section instrument.
Like drums used to be. When did all these drum solos --
Ever since I can remember the drum solos.
Yeah. They get awfully popular in the mid-thirties.
